checklist.summary: File and serve the motion before requesting a hearing by email to the assistant, copying all parties and supplying case number, motion, counsel names and time requested. Email cancellations even if a notice was filed; only the scheduling party may cancel the motion hearing.

Certify opposing counsel/party received the motion and that good-faith conferral occurred. Keep the assistant out of interparty date-coordination emails; email the assistant for dates and final confirmation.

Request a OneDrive link from the assistant, copying all parties. Submit hearing materials at least three business days before the hearing. Hard copies are a fallback only if using the drop box is impossible and must arrive by that deadline. Do not email copies of hearing documents.

Ordinarily use the circuit e-filing portal with a PDF cover letter stating agreement or at least seven days without a response. Contested orders are excluded from that route: contact the office to schedule a hearing; try to resolve disagreements, and if unresolved email each proposed order and a copy highlighting disputed portions to the assistant. checklist.summary: Request hearing time by email to Brittany Smith, copying opposing counsel, using the Bay case number/style in the subject and supplying the motion, time needed and counsel details. Clear and confirm dates; await assistant confirmation before filing the hearing notice and email the filed notice. Use Central Time; keep the assistant out of interparty scheduling chains. Short motion-calendar hearings require reserved/confirmed slots; the source excludes jury-trial weeks and shifts Monday holidays to Tuesday.

The source requires good-faith certification for most motions and describes its requirement as broader than Rule 1.202. An unanswered email alone is insufficient; it calls for at least two calls in the stated no-response circumstances. Exceptions cover truly dispositive motions, emergencies preventing attempted contact (not delay-created emergencies), and posttrial/postjudgment motions; technical dismissal motions likely permitting amendment still require conferral. No determination of controlling authority is made.

Request a OneDrive folder with email addresses for all parties/counsel needing access; upload separate PDFs, not ZIP files. Do not email hearing documents. Page12 states materials and folder requests at least two business days before hearing, but paragraph2h says uploads complete one business day before. Page12 prohibits mailed hardcopies unless the assistant directs; page13 permits hardcopy when OneDrive is impossible with receipt two business days before. These differing statements are preserved without reconciliation.

Submit Word orders through the portal in the specified DJCMA format, omitting the assistant service-certification portions, with a PDF cover letter stating agreement status and no hidden formatting. Only cover letter/order ordinarily go through that route, with the stated pretrial-stipulation witness/exhibit-list exception. Preserve the required service paragraph and counsel service responsibility for unregistered parties; the office does not mail orders.

The guide addresses hearing materials rather than a separate named courtesy-copy procedure. Documents already accessible in the court file ordinarily need not be resubmitted; preserve the exception for incorporated or hard-to-identify documents. Follow the qualified OneDrive/hardcopy instructions above.

Motion-calendar hearings use Zoom. For matters not yet set as of the source update, specially set hearings are in person unless the court grants Zoom permission; an out-of-county office alone is not grounds. The Zoom instructions apply only to scheduled/permitted Zoom appearances and require video unless impossible, with login five minutes early.

Email cancellations promptly to the assistant; a court-ordered trial or hearing cannot be cancelled merely by filing notice without court approval. Where the case’s standing order requires certification of reading the order and procedures, follow that order’s time periods. Do not infer a separate assistant telephone from the office number.

Communications with the Judicial Office 
 
A. 
Method of Communication 
 
1. 
All communications to the judicial office must be submitted by e-

subject line of any e-mail to the judicial assistant must contain 
the case name and case number (e.g., Doe v. Doe, 25CA1234). 
 
2.

service may communicate with the judicial office by telephone 
call to 850-638-6255. The judicial office does not accept text

Unsolicited Communication

Parties may only contact the judicial office in accordance with

from non-parties will not be considered by the court.

mail address to receive signed orders electronically, unless

responsibility of attorneys and self-represented litigants to 
update their contact information through the Clerk’s office using 
Form 2.603 any time there is a change in the e-mail account 
registered for electronic service.

C. 
Certificate of Good Faith Conferral 
 
1. 
Before filing any motion, except as noted in Fla. R. Civ. P. 1.202, 
the moving party shall confer with counsel for the opposing party 
in a good faith effort to resolve the issues raised by the motion, 
and the motion shall contain a statement certifying that the 
moving party has conferred with opposing counsel and that 
counsel have been unable to agree on the resolution of the motion 
(the “Certificate”). 
 
2. 
The term “confer” as used herein, means a substantive 
conversation either in person or by telephone in a good faith effort 
to resolve the motion without court action and does not envision 
an exchange of ultimatums by e-mail, fax, or letter. Certification 
that counsel has attempted to confer with opposing counsel is 
not sufficient. The court may sua sponte deny motions that fail 
to include an appropriate and complete certificate under this 
section. 
 
3. 
The certificate shall set forth the date of the conference, the 
names of the participating attorneys, and the specific results 
achieved. It shall be the responsibility of counsel for the movant 
to arrange for the conference. Counsel are expected to respond 
promptly to inquiries and communication from opposing counsel. 
Repeated failure or refusal of a party or attorney to so confer 
should be set out with specificity in the certificate. 
 
4. 
No conference, therefore, no certificate, is required for 
appropriate ex parte motions, uncontested motions, judgment on 
the pleadings, summary judgment, or other dispositive motions. 
 
5. 
A party alleging that a pleading fails to state a cause of action will 
confer with counsel for the opposing party before moving to 
dismiss, and, upon request of the other party will stipulate to an 
order permitting the filing of a curative amended pleading in lieu 
of filing a motion to dismiss.

General Procedures 
 
1. Verify Judge J. Patterson is the judge assigned to the case.

opposing counsel.  These requests should be made via email to dixond@jud14.flcourts.org. 
Use Bay or Gulf County case number and style of case as your subject line.

a. Type of motion(s) to be heard 
b. Actual amount of time needed for counsel to argue motion(s) 
c. First date movant is available for hearing (see #7 below) 
d. Names of attorneys that will attend hearing 
e. Attach copy of the motion(s) to the email

have sufficient time for the hearing may result in the motion or request being denied or the 
hearing continued.

instructions.  READ ENTIRE EMAIL.  Be aware that Bay County in the central time 
zone and Gulf County is in the eastern time zone.

1. For short motion hearings (15 minutes or less), motion calendar docket will be maintained 
by the Court. 
 
2. It is anticipated that counsel may set hearings on a motion calendar docket with one or two 
weeks of advanced notice. 
 
3. Follow the procedures contained in the General Procedures on Page 2 (to include emailing 
the judicial assistant for available motion calendar dockets, clearing the hearing time with 
opposing counsel, confirming the date and providing a copy of the notice of hearing).  Slots 
on each motion calendar docket are limited.  Slots on a particular motion calendar docket 
will be given on a first come, first confirmed basis. 
 
4.  All matters set on the motion calendar docket should be noticed to start at 9:30am or 
1:00pm (to coincide with each time zone). 
 
5. The case/motion will be called in order that the motions are set for hearing. 
 
6. The motion calendar is intended to hear short, simple motions on an expedited basis to keep 
a case moving (15-minute or less hearings).  If extensive argument occurs, the hearing will 
be continued to a later time, to be set for a certain time under the General Procedures on 
page 2.  Accordingly, DO NOT try to set a matter on the motion calendar that cannot be 
concluded withing 15 minutes as it will delay the conclusion of the hearing on the motion 
and annoy the other attorneys set for hearing on the motion calendar.  If there is an abuse of 
the motion calendar docket by a particular attorney or law firm, it may result in the 
attorney/law firm not being able to set matters on the motion calendar in the future.

Civil – Good Faith Certification for Motions 
 
1. For most motions (other than truly dispositive motions), the moving party is required to 
include a certification in the motion that the movant made a “good faith attempt” to resolve 
the issue(s) raised in the motion with the opposing counsel or party (whether represented or 
pro se) prior to filing the motion.  This Court’s requirement of conferral is broader than that 
included in Rule 1.202, Florida Rules of Civil Procedure. 
 
2. A “good faith attempt” is not satisfied by the movant sending one or two emails to the 
opposing counsel or party if pro se and claiming no response was received.  Movant may 
initiate the “good faith attempt” via email.  However, if no response is received, the movant 
shall call the opposing counsel’s office or party at least twice if no response is received to an 
email or initial phone call before certifying that the movant has made a “good faith attempt” 
to resolve the issue(s) raised in the motion. 
 
3. The judicial assistant may reject offering hearing time if a motion does not include 
certification of a “good faith attempt” to resolve the issue(s) in the motion prior to filing the 
motion. 
 
4. The only circumstances where a “good faith attempt” certification is not required is for 
dispositive motions (motions to dismiss with prejudice, motions for judgment on the 
pleadings, motions for summary judgment, etc.), emergency motions where the movant is 
not able to attempt contact because of the circumstances (however, delaying filing a motion 
that could be filed earlier is not considered an emergency just because the deadline is 
approaching), and post-trial or post-judgment motions (such as motions for rehearing or 
reconsideration).  For motions to dismiss that raise primarily technical issues which, under 
applicable law would likely result in the pleading party being given leave to amend, the 
movant shall make a “good faith attempt” to resolve the issue(s) before filing the motion 
(e.g., where a party omits a copy of a contract or document from the complaint in an action 
for breach of contract).

1. In the event of the cancellation of a hearing, please notify the judicial assistant as promptly 
as possible to open the time for other cases. 
 
2. In the event of a settlement or dismissal of a case set for trial, please notify the judicial 
assistant that the matter has settled or been dismissed so that it can be removed from the trial 
docket, even if there are still matters remaining to be concluded (filing dismissal, signing of 
agreed upon settlement agreement, exchange of payment, etc.).  However, if a settlement is 
contingent upon the agreement to the form of an agreement and/or release, please wait until 
the language of the agreement and/or release is agreed to by all parties prior to requesting a 
matter be removed from the trial docket. 
 
3. Notices to the judicial assistant of a cancellation, settlement or dismissal should be sent via 
email.

settlement or dismissal, the matter will be removed from the calendar.  It is suggested that 
counsel file and serve a notice of cancellation of a hearing, and upon filing, send a copy via 
email to the judicial assistant. 
 
5. Counsel and parties may not cancel a trial or hearing scheduled by Court Order by simply 
filing a notice of cancellation without obtaining approval of the Court.

Communication

a. Do NOT call the judge’s office to request hearing time or to inquire as to the status of

2. Ex Parte 
a. All communications with the judicial office must comply with Canon 3 of the Code of 
Judicial Conduct, which prohibits a judge from initiating, permitting, or considering ex 
parte communications and from considering other communications outside the presence of 
the parties concerning a pending or impending proceeding, unless authorized by law. All 
parties must be copied on any e-mail directed to the judicial office, unless an ex parte 
communication is authorized by law. 
 
3. Unsolicited 
a. Unsolicited communications from non-parties will not be considered by the Court. Parties 
may only contact the judicial office in accordance with these practices and procedures.

Hearing Time 
 
1. Scheduling 
a. The Judge’s scheduling calendar is not available online. Hearing requests must be made in 
accordance with Paragraph 1(a) above and have a copy of the motion(s) attached to the

b. The Judge’s office does not hold hearing dates. A hearing is not scheduled on the Court’s 
calendar unless you receive confirmation from the judicial assistant. 
c. Ensure accuracy in the amount of time needed for the hearing. The Court will not extend 
hearing time if the parties did not request enough time and the matter will be continued to 
a future hearing date. 
d. The judicial assistant will “reply all” to the email with available dates, times and 
instructions.  NOTE: Bay County is in the central time zone.   
e. In the event counsel cannot agree on a mutually convenient date and time for the hearing 
from the dates and times provided, the Court may unilaterally set the matter for hearing

2  
 
or alternatively enter an order on the matter without hearing.  If the Court unilaterally 
sets the matter for hearing, the hearing cannot be canceled without a Court order.   
f. If the parties resolve the issue prior to the Court-scheduled hearing, they shall submit an 
agreed upon proposed order more than one (1) business day prior to hearing date to avoid 
the requirement for appearance at the Court-scheduled hearing.  Accordingly, to the extent 
possible, counsel should seek another attorney from their office to cover a hearing to avoid 
either having no choice in the date and time of a hearing or waiving a hearing on the matter.  
g. Only email the judicial assistant to request dates and confirm the hearing date. Do not 
include the judicial assistant in email chains between counsel and/or staff to clear dates (or 
anything else).  
h. If a pro se party is involved in the case, an attempt should be made to coordinate the hearing 
date and time with the pro se party.  If counsel receives no response to an initial attempt to 
coordinate with the pro se party after two (2) business days, counsel may unilaterally set 
the hearing.  
 
2. Notices 
a. DO NOT file a notice of hearing before receiving a confirmation email from the judicial 
assistant confirming that the hearing has been set.   
b. Email the judicial assistant a copy of all notices for hearing once filed.   
c. Any motions noticed, but not specifically scheduled with the judicial assistant, will not be 
heard.

a. Additional motions cannot be piggybacked on a previously scheduled hearing time without 
being cleared with the judicial assistant and opposing counsel, and such motions may only 
potentially be added if sufficient time has been reserved. Do not prepare and file a notice

b. Notice Content: 
i. Physical Address:  300 E. 4th Street, Panama City, FL 32401.  There is no room number

citations.quote:
Good Faith Certification for Motions 
1. For most motions (other than truly dispositive motions), the moving party is required to include 
a certification in the motion that movant made a “good faith attempt” to resolve the issue(s) 
raised in the motion with the opposing counsel or party (whether represented or pro se) prior 
to filing the motion.  This Court’s requirement of conferral is broader than that included in 
Rule 1.202, Florida Rules of Civil Procedure. 
2. A “good faith attempt” is not satisfied by the movant sending one or two emails to the opposing 
counsel or party if pro se and claiming no response was received.  Movant may initiate the 
“good faith attempt” via email.  However, if no response is received, the movant shall call the 
opposing counsel’s office or party at least twice if no response is received to an email or initial 
phone call before certifying that the movant has made a “good faith attempt” to resolve the 
issue(s) raised in the motion. 
3. The judicial assistant may reject offering hearing time if a motion does not include certification 
of a “good faith attempt” to resolve the issue(s) in the motion prior to filing the motion. 
4. The only circumstances where a “good faith attempt” certification is not required is for 
dispositive motions (motions to dismiss with prejudice, motions for judgment on the pleadings, 
motions for summary judgment, etc.), emergency motions where the movant is not able to 
attempt contact because of the circumstances (however, delaying filing a motion that could be 
filed earlier is not considered an emergency just because the deadline is approaching), and 
post-trial or post-judgment motions (such as motions for rehearing or reconsideration).  For 
motions to dismiss that raise primarily technical issues which, under applicable law would 
likely result in the pleading party being given leave to amend, the movant shall make a “good 
faith attempt” to resolve the issue(s) before filing the motion (e.g., where a party omits a copy 
of a contract or document from the complaint in an action for breach of contract).

1. If a party intends on presenting any evidence or documents (including memos and caselaw) to

parties prior to the hearing no less than five (5) days before the hearing.

a. Exhibits  
b. Memoranda not previously filed with the clerk

However, additional copies of motions, memoranda already filed with the clerk or other

Cancellations

the judicial assistant as promptly as possible to open the time for other cases and provide a 
copy of the Notice of Cancellation. Hearings set by the Court cannot be canceled by the parties 
without requesting approval to do so from the Court. 
2. In the event of a settlement or dismissal of a case set for trial, please notify the judicial assistant 
that the matter has settled or been dismissed so it can be removed from the trial docket, even 
if there are still matters remaining to be concluded (filing dismissal, signing of agreed upon 
settlement agreement, exchange of payment, etc.).  However, if a settlement is contingent upon 
the agreement to the form of an agreement and/or release, please wait until the language of the 
agreement and/or release is agreed to by all parties prior to requesting a matter be removed 
from the trial docket. 
3. Upon receipt by the judicial assistant of the email canceling a hearing or notifying of a 
settlement or dismissal, the matter will be removed from the calendar.

Civil – Hearing Time 
General Procedures 
1. Verify Judge Smith is the judge assigned to the case. 
 
2. PLEASE NOTE, for any matter that has not been set for hearing as of the effective 
date of this update, all hearings will be held IN PERSON (not via Zoom) at the Bay 
County Courthouse, unless the Court specifically grants a request to appear 
remotely (via Zoom).  Just because an attorney’s office may be located outside of 
Bay County is not grounds to request to appear via Zoom.   
 
3. DO NOT call the judge’s office to request hearing a time. 
 
4. Email any request for hearing time to Judge Smith’s assistant, Kealani Daniels, and CC 
opposing counsel.  These requests can be sent to danielsk@jud14.flcourts.org.  Use Bay 
County case number and style of case as your subject line 
 
5. Provide the following information in the hearing time request email: 
a. Type of motion(s) to be heard 
b. If a remote hearing is requested 
c. Actual amount of time needed for counsel to argue motion(s) 
d. Names of attorneys that will attend hearing 
e. Attach a copy of the motion(s) to the email 
 
6. Please be accurate in the amount of time needed for the hearing.  Failure to have 
sufficient time for the hearing may result in the motion or request being denied or the 
hearing continued. 
 
7. Most motions, except dispositive motions, should be set for hearing within sixty (60) 
days of being filed, with simpler motions (such as motions to compel) being set for 
hearing within thirty (30) days of filing.  Failure to timely set a hearing on a motion may 
result in the motion being summarily denied without hearing. 
 
8. The judicial assistant will “reply all” to the email with available dates, times and 
instructions.  READ ENTIRE EMAIL.  Be aware that Bay County is in the central 
time zone.  All hearing times are in thirty (30) minute increments and shall be noticed for 
central time zone. 
 
9. The judicial assistant will provide up to six (6) dates and times for a hearing.  IN THE 
EVENT COUNSEL CANNOT AGREE on a mutually convenient date and time for the 
hearing from the dates and times provided, the Court may unilaterally set the matter 
for hearing or alternatively enter an order on the matter without hearing.  If the 
Court unilaterally sets the matter for hearing, the hearing cannot be canceled without a 
Court order.  If the parties resolve the issue prior to the Court-scheduled hearing, they 
shall submit an agreed upon proposed order more than one (1) business day prior to 
hearing date to avoid the requirement for appearance at the Court-scheduled hearing.

citations.quote:
--- PAGE 3 ---
3 
 
Accordingly, to the extent possible, counsel should seek another attorney from their 
office to cover a hearing to avoid either having no choice in the date and time of a 
hearing or waiving a hearing on the matter. 
 
10. Only email the judicial assistant to request dates and confirm the hearing date.  DO NOT 
include the judicial assistant in email chains between counsel and/or staff to clear dates 
(or anything else). 
 
11. If a pro se party is involved in the case, an attempt should be made to coordinate the 
hearing date and time with the pro se party.  If counsel receives no response to an initial 
attempt to coordinate with the pro se party after two (2) business days, counsel may 
unilaterally set the hearing. 
 
12. DO NOT file a notice of hearing before receiving a confirmation email from the judicial 
assistant confirming that the hearing has been calendared. 
 
13. Email the judicial assistant a copy of all notices for hearing once filed. 
 
14. Any motions noticed, but not scheduled and confirmed with the judicial assistant, will not 
be heard. 
 
15. Additional motions cannot be piggybacked on a previously scheduled hearing time 
without being cleared with the judicial assistant and opposing counsel, and such motions 
may only potentially be added if sufficient time has been reserved.  To add a motion to a 
previously scheduled hearing, obtain opposing counsel’s consent to the addition, then 
email the judicial assistant about adding the motion to the hearing and advise if 
additional time is required.  The judicial assistant will confirm the addition of the 
motion to the hearing time.  If additional time is required but not available, the request to 
piggyback a motion will be denied and the motion will need to be reset at a different date 
and time.  Do not prepare and file a notice of the added motion until receipt of the 
judicial assistant’s confirmation. 
 
16. Address:  300 E. 4th Street, Panama City, FL 32401.  There is no room number – just list 
as Judge Smith’s Chambers.   
 
17. The parties may stipulate to having a motion decided without the necessity of a hearing.  
If such is the case, the movant shall include at least a brief memorandum of law as part of 
the motion being filed or as a supplemental filing on the motion.  Thereafter, the 
nonmovant shall file a response which shall include at least a brief memorandum of law 
as part of the response.  Upon filing of the response, the movant’s counsel shall contact 
the judicial assistant and advise that a non-hearing motion and response have been filed 
and provide copies of the filed motion and response.  The Court shall consider the motion 
and response and issue a ruling.

--- PAGE 4 ---
4 
 
Civil – Good Faith Certification for Motions  
 
1. For most motions (other than truly dispositive motions), the moving party is required to 
include a certification in the motion that counsel made a “good faith attempt” to resolve 
the issue(s) raised in the motion with opposing counsel prior to filing the motion. 
 
2. A “good faith attempt” is not satisfied by counsel sending one or two emails to opposing 
counsel and claiming no response was received.  Counsel may initiate the “good faith 
attempt” via email.  However, if no response is received, counsel shall call opposing 
counsel’s office at least twice if no response is received to an email or initial phone call 
before certifying that counsel has made a “good faith attempt” to resolve the issue(s) 
raised in the motion. 
 
3. The judicial assistant may reject offering hearing time if a motion does not include 
certification of a “good faith attempt” to resolve the issue(s) in the motion prior to filing 
the motion. 
 
4. The only circumstances where a “good faith attempt” certification is not required is for 
dispositive motions (motions to dismiss with prejudice, motions for judgment on the 
pleadings, motions for summary judgment, etc.), emergency motions where counsel is 
not able to attempt contact because of the circumstances (however, counsel delaying 
filing a motion that could be filed earlier is not considered an emergency just because the 
deadline is approaching), and post-trial or post-judgment motions (such as motions for 
rehearing or reconsideration).  For motions to dismiss that raise primarily technical issues 
which, under applicable law would likely result in the pleading party being given leave to 
amend, counsel shall make a “good faith attempt” to resolve the issue(s) before filing the 
motion (e.g., where a party omits a copy of a contract or document from the complaint in 
an action for breach of contract).

7. As a video Zoom conference hearing is a court proceeding, counsel and any party 
attending a hearing will be properly attired and behave as if appearing in person in court. 
 
8. So that hearings can promptly start, please log into the Zoom video conference at least

--- PAGE 8 ---
8 
 
Civil – Submission of Proposed Orders 
 
1. All proposed orders must be submitted via the e-filing portal or via email if a request 
for such is granted by Judge Smith.  
 
2. All proposed orders must include a cover letter in .pdf format.  The cover letter 
should indicate whether the proposed order is agreed to by opposing counsel/party or 
not. 
 
3. Only the cover letter and proposed order should be submitted via the e-filing 
portal.  Copies of motions, responses, exhibits, case law or other items should not be 
included with the cover letter or uploaded in the e-filing portal (see Submission of 
Hearing Materials, infra).   
 
4. All proposed orders must be submitted in Word format.  Counsel and parties 
preparing orders are directed to remove any hidden formatting or codes.  Failure 
to remove hidden formatting may result in the order being rejected. 
 
5. All proposed orders must be in DJCMA format (see #6 & 7 below), but 
counsel/parties are directed to omit the service portion for the judicial assistant 
to sign and certify service of the order (the M and A portions of the DJCMA 
format). 
 
6. Proposed orders do not need to include the addresses or email addresses of recipients 
of the order at the end.  A copy of the signed order will be served on all 
counsel/parties registered for service via the e-portal.   
 
7. If the case involves a pro se party who is not registered to receive filings from the e-
portal, the proposed order shall include as the last paragraph (before DONE AND 
ORDERED) the following statement: 
 
Counsel who submitted this proposed order to the Court for 
approval shall serve a copy of this Order on any party not registered 
to receive service via the Court’s e-portal. 
 
Counsel receiving the served copy of an order entered is then charged with 
responsibility for serving (via mail or email) a copy of the signed order on any party 
not registered to receive service via the e-portal.  The judge’s office will not mail out 
copies of any orders. 
 
8. A memo with instructions on submission of proposed orders and the DJCMA format 
can be accessed at:  Microsoft Word - Memo-Submission of Proposed Orders to 
Judiciary.doc (flcourts.org)

--- PAGE 10 ---
10 
 
Civil – Submission of Hearing Materials 
(Pleadings, Memoranda, Exhibits, Case Law) 
 
1. Any documentation being used or relied upon at a hearing that a party wants the 
Court to review and consider must be submitted at least two (2) business days 
prior to the date of the hearing.  This includes: 
 
a. Exhibits 
b. Memoranda not previously filed with the clerk 
c. Copies of case law, statutes or other citations 
d. Any demonstrative aides 
e. Any other documentation that a party intends to use at the hearing 
However, additional copies of motions, memoranda already filed with the 
clerk or other documents which are already in the court file (unless attached 
to or incorporated in other filings and not easily accessible or identifiable) DO 
NOT need to be submitted again prior to the hearing. 
2. In lieu of hard copies of hearing materials, all hearing materials should be 
submitted via Microsoft OneDrive drop box.  DO NOT MAIL HARD COPIES 
OR A BINDER OF CASE LAW OR OTHER HEARING MATERIALS 
unless specifically directed by the judicial assistant.  The procedures for obtaining 
the drop box are: 
 
a. Any counsel or party that desires to provide hearing materials shall contact 
the judicial assistant and request a OneDrive drop box for the case at least 
two (2) business days prior to the hearing.  Please be sure to include the 
email addresses of all parties/counsel who require access.  The judicial 
assistant will send out an email to all parties with a link to the drop box.  
b. Either the movant or party opposing the motion may submit documents to 
the drop box 
c. Please label the documents submitted to the drop box so that they can be 
easily identified 
d. Any case law or other items being submitted should be uploaded as 
separate .pdf documents 
e. DO NOT upload documents as a zip file/folder as the Court will be unable 
to access those 
f. If documents being submitted include exhibits for an evidentiary hearing, 
please premark the exhibits and identify the party intending to introduce 
the exhibit.  Counsel should agree on the method being used to identify the 
exhibits (such as one side using numbers and the opposing side using 
letters, or using party ID before the number/letter). 
g. Counsel are responsible for redacting ALL confidential information 
on any document that will be offered into evidence. 
h. All uploaded documents must be completed one (1) business day prior to 
the hearing.

citations.quote:
--- PAGE 12 ---
12 
 
Civil – Cancellations 
 
1. In the event of a cancellation of a hearing, please notify the judicial assistant as promptly 
as possible to open the time for other cases. 
 
2. In the event of a settlement of a case set for trial, please notify the judicial assistant that 
the matter has settled so it can be removed from the trial docket, even if there are still 
matters remaining to be concluded (filing dismissal, signing of agreed upon settlement 
agreement, exchange of payment, etc.).  However, if a settlement is contingent upon the 
agreement to the form of an agreement and/or release, please wait until the language of 
the agreement and/or release is agreed to by all parties prior to requesting a matter be 
removed from the trial docket. 
 
3. Notices to the judicial assistant of a cancellation or settlement should be sent via email. 
 
4. Upon receipt by the judicial assistant of the email canceling a hearing or notifying of a 
settlement, the matter will be removed from the calendar.  It is suggested that counsel file 
and serve a notice of cancellation of a hearing, and upon filing, send a copy via email to 
the judicial assistant.   
 
5. Counsel and parties cannot cancel a hearing scheduled by Court Order by simply filing a 
notice of cancellation without getting approval of the Court.

Courthouse Security 
2025-00-15 
(Rescinding AO # 2025-00-14) 
 
Page 1
 
 
IN THE CIRCUIT COURT OF THE FOURTEENTH JUDICIAL CIRCUIT 
Bay, Calhoun, Gulf, Holmes, Jackson, and Washington Counties 
THE STATE OF FLORIDA 
 
ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER #2025-00-15 
(Rescinding Administrative Order #2025-00-14) 
 
RE: COURTHOUSE SECURITY 
 
WHEREAS increased threats and acts of violence directed at witnesses, jurors, litigants, 
lawyers, court personnel, and judges throughout our nation and locally demonstrate the need for 
additional security at our county courthouses, courthouse annexes, and any “off-site” courtrooms 
or office buildings in the Fourteenth Judicial Circuit. 
 
WHEREAS, the protection of the public, the jurors, and courthouse personnel is of the 
utmost concern of the judges of the Fourteenth Judicial Circuit, and by such, a major component 
of a prompt and efficient administration of justice is preserved. 
 
WHEREAS, pursuant to Article V, Section 2(d) of the Florida Constitution, section 43.26, 
Florida Statutes, and Rule 2.215(b)(2) and (7), Florida Rules of General Practice and Judicial 
Administration, establishes that the chief judge of a circuit shall exercise administrative 
supervision over all courts within the judicial circuit, and “shall regulate the use of all court 
facilities”; and 
 
WHEREAS Rule 2.215(b)(3) and (6), Florida Rules of General Practice and Judicial 
Administration, directs the chief judge to develop an administrative plan for the efficient and 
proper administration of all courts within the circuit and accordingly finds it necessary and 
appropriate to establish responsibilities and guidelines related to courthouse security; and 
 
WHEREAS, section 29.008(1)(e), Florida Statutes, requires counties to fund the cost of 
security of facilities for the circuit and county courts including the security needs of such buildings 
and other court related functions. 
 
NOW, THEREFORE, it is ORDERED and ADJUDGED that the following procedures 
concerning courthouse security shall be followed: 
 
I. 
General Provisions 
 
ALL PERSONS, with the exception of those specifically enumerated in Section II of this 
Order, shall be prohibited from carrying or possessing firearms, antique or replica firearms, 
weapons, or destructive devices, as defined in section 790.001, Florida Statutes, in a courthouse, 

--- PAGE 2 ---
Courthouse Security 
2025-00-15 
(Rescinding AO # 2025-00-14) 
 
Page 2
 
courthouse annex, “off-site” courthouse office building or courtroom (hereinafter collectively 
referred to as the “courthouse”) in the six counties of the Fourteenth Judicial Circuit. Further, ALL 
PERSONS are prohibited from carrying or being in possession of any other device(s) or 
instrument(s) that could be used or perceived to be used as a physical threat to persons or property 
in the courthouses of the Fourteenth Judicial Circuit. 
 
Prohibitions may include, but are not limited to, the following: 
 
• 
Pocket knives of any size. 
• 
Scissors. 
• 
Firearms, stun guns, long guns, or any item which shoots a projectile. 
• 
Ammunition. 
• 
Fireworks. 
• 
Flammable liquids. 
 
To enforce the prohibition, each Sheriff and his/her appointed deputies or bailiff are 
empowered to stop all persons entering the courthouses to conduct a security search. Security 
equipment, purchased by funds provided by the county, which will allow for the scanning of person 
and of property in the least intrusive means practicable should be used to assist the deputies and 
bailiffs to determine the person’s compliance with the administrative order and ensure the safety 
of the occupants of the courthouse. The discovery of illegal weapons, contraband as defined in 
Section 932.701, Florida Statutes, or other violations of criminal statutes will result in the 
immediate notification of law enforcement so that an arrest and seizure can be made. 
 
The prohibition of carrying weapons into a court facility supersedes any local law, 
ordinance or local rule that may otherwise authorize possession of a weapon or firearm in a county-
owned facility. 
 
Persons refusing to submit to a search of their person and effects shall be denied access 
into the courthouse. 
 
II. 
Exempt Persons 
 
The following individuals are exempt from the prohibition against carrying FIREARMS 
into the courthouse, based on their job, position, and duties. However, such persons SHALL NOT 
carry firearms into the courthouse if the purpose of their visit to the courthouse is personal. 
 
• 
All certified law enforcement officers, including federal, state, county, and city, while 
on official law enforcement business. 
• 
Active and Senior Judges; and 
• 
Magistrates and Hearing Officers licensed to carry a concealed weapon of firearm 
pursuant to section 790.06, Florida Statutes; and 
• 
Clerks and Evidence Custodians according to their policies; and 
• 
Contracted Armored Car Personnel; and 
• 
Marshalls and Judges from the Florida Supreme Court and First District Court of 
Appeal; and 

--- PAGE 3 ---
Courthouse Security 
2025-00-15 
(Rescinding AO # 2025-00-14) 
 
Page 3
 
• 
14th Circuit State Attorney, Assistant State Attorneys and Investigators.  However, 
under no circumstances are they permitted to carry firearms into a judge’s chambers, 
court administration offices, clerks’ offices or other hearing rooms; and 
• 
Any person deemed by a presiding judge authorized to carry a concealed weapon or 
firearm in his/her courtroom, per section 790.06 (12) (a) 5, Florida Statutes.  Prior 
notice must be given to the presiding judge and court security before anyone is 
approved to carry a firearm or other weapon. 
• 
Unless otherwise directed by the Chief Judge, all judges, judicial assistants and court 
administration employees are authorized to carry tasers, pepper spray or other non-
lethal but otherwise lawful personal protection devices inside court facilities. 
 
Exceptional or Emergency Circumstances 
At their discretion, and Sheriffs of the 14th Judicial Circuit may temporarily prohibit any 
persons authorized by this administrative order from carrying weapons into a court facility. 
 
III. 
Admission Searches 
 
A. 
Any person (excluding courthouse personnel entering the secured personnel 
entrance) desiring to enter the courthouse shall enter through the authorized entrance 
and pass through security equipment (e.g., magnetometer) where available or scanned 
by a hand-held scanning device. 
 
B. 
Any person who activates the security equipment will be asked to empty his/her 
pockets and to pass through the security device a second time. If, after this second 
review, security concerns remain, the person shall be subject to a more thorough 
search to identify all objects which activated the security equipment. 
 
C. 
Any person, prior to passing through any security equipment, shall place any purse, 
package, briefcase, wallet, computer or other electronic equipment, or any other item 
into the container provided and allow the equipment to either be physically inspected 
by the security officer or scanned by the security equipment. 
 
D. 
Any person with a pacemaker, internal cardiac defibrillator, or other such device 
should notify the security officer and present a medical card confirming such so that 
the person can avoid the magnetometer (if being used). The person will then be 
subject to security checks which may include use of a hand-held device. 
 
E. 
If illegal firearms, weapons, destructive devices, or contraband as defined above are 
found during a search, an arrest and seizure may occur. 
 
F. 
All courthouse personnel shall either enter through the separate secured personnel 
entrance (if applicable) or, if they choose to enter through the main entrance, must 
show courthouse ID badge bearing their photo, to avoid security screening. 
 
 
 

--- PAGE 4 ---
Courthouse Security 
2025-00-15 
(Rescinding AO # 2025-00-14) 
 
Page 4
 
IV. 
Notice 
 
One of the following two notices shall be posted in a conspicuous place at all courthouse 
entrances where applicable: 
 
FOR THE PROTECTION OF THE PUBLIC 
 
All Persons and Personal Belongings Entering the Courthouse Will be Searched. No

Video Conferencing
Remote Court Appearances via Zoom
Overview
Many court proceedings can now be attended remotely using Zoom, a secure video conferencing platform. This guide provides instructions to help you prepare for and participate in a remote court appearance.
Receiving Your Zoom Link
Court Notice
: The Zoom link for your scheduled court appearance will be included in your official Court Notice.
Judicial Assistant
: Alternatively, the Judge's Judicial Assistant may provide the Zoom link directly. Contact the court if you have not received the link at least 24 hours before your scheduled appearance.
Preparing for Your Remote Appearance
Technology Requirements
:
A stable internet connection.
A device with a camera, microphone, and speakers (computer, tablet, or smartphone).
The Zoom application installed on your device. Download it for free at zoom.us/download.
Test Your Setup
:
Test your audio and video in advance using Zoom's test meeting feature: zoom.us/test.
Ensure your device is fully charged or plugged in.
Environment
:
Choose a quiet, well-lit location with a neutral background.
Avoid public spaces to maintain privacy and minimize distractions.
Dress in appropriate courtroom attire (business casual or formal).
Joining the Zoom Hearing
Access the Meeting
:
Click the Zoom link provided in your Court Notice or by the Judicial Assistant.
If prompted, enter the Meeting ID and Passcode included in the link or notice.
Before Joining
:
Enter your full legal name as it appears on your case documents to ensure proper identification.
Mute your microphone and turn off your camera until instructed by the court.
During the Hearing
:
Follow the Judge's instructions regarding when to unmute or turn on your camera.
Speak clearly and avoid interrupting others.
Do not record or take screenshots of the proceeding, as this may violate court rules.
Technical Support
If you encounter issues with Zoom, visit support.zoom.us for troubleshooting.
Courtroom Etiquette
Treat the remote appearance with the same respect as an in-person court session.
Address the Judge as "Your Honor" and follow all court instructions.
Avoid eating, drinking, or engaging in other activities during the hearing.
Additional Resources
For Zoom tutorials, visit zoom.us/resources.
